newsitem.title: UK: Novorossiisk reopens but two berths shut for repair.
newsitem.headline: Novorossiisk reopens but two berths shut for repair.

text.p: The Russian oil port of Novorossiisk reopened late on Tuesday after a 64-hour closure due to high winds, but two of the port's berths are now closed for scheduled maintenance, a shipping source said.
The Black Sea port reopened at 2050 local time on Tuesday after bad weather forced closure early on Sunday morning.
Berths two and three were closed this week until May 26 for scheduled maintenance. Berth two loads crude tankers of 80,000 to 90,000 tonnes, and berth three is a small products berth.
The crude tanker Superlady berthed at the main berth one on Wednesday morning, about two days behind schedule, and two other tankers were waiting at anchor, the shipping source said.
"By the time the others have loaded things should be back to normal," the source said.
The Baltic port of Ventspils was also open to tanker traffic on Wednesday, but the main crude pipeline feeding the port was closed as tank storage was full.
The other Black Sea oil ports of Odessa and Tuapse were operating normally, the source said.
